snippet.title: How Shawn Fonteno Outsmarted Rockstar
snippet.description:
Shawn Fonteno, also known as Solo118, was born April 8, 1968, in Watts, Los Angeles. Before becoming famous as the voice of Franklin Clinton in Grand Theft Auto V, Shawn lived a real street life. He joined the 118 East Coast Crips, a well-known set of the East Coast Crip umbrella in South Central Los Angeles. The East Coast Crips are one of the largest Crip factions in LA, made up of multiple sets that hold territory across the East Side. The 118s in particular have a long history in Watts and surrounding areas, known for their ties to the streets, rivalries, and the culture that shaped much of LA gang life.

Shawn’s past in the 118 East Coast Crips gave him a firsthand look at the realities of gang culture, but it also became part of the story he would later flip into something bigger. From surviving the dangers of the streets to stepping into Hollywood and the gaming world, his journey shows both the struggle and the change.

He’s not just Franklin from GTA — he’s an actor, rapper, and author whose memoir, Game Changer: My Journey From the Streets to Your Video Game Console, lays out his life from the hood to the spotlight.

snippet.title: GTA 5's Franklin actor says Kai Cenat reached out after promise controversy.
snippet.description:
The briefest celebrity feud of the GTA cycle is already over. Shawn "Solo" Fonteno, the voice behind Franklin Clinton in Grand Theft Auto V, went viral after accusing Kai Cenat of breaking a promise to a young fan. But just a day later, the two squared it away.
The Original Accusation
On the Dope As Usual podcast, Fonteno recounted a 2024 stream where he took Kai Cenat through the real Los Angeles neighborhoods that inspired GTA 5's Los Santos. During the outing, they visited a struggling family around 15 people in a one-bedroom home. A young boy asked Kai for a motorcycle, and Kai allegedly told him, "We gon' make it happen" .
Fonteno said Kai then ignored his calls and texts for weeks. The bike would have cost roughly $1,000 to $1,200. "If I make a promise, especially to a kid, I'ma honor it," Fonteno said .
The Resolution
On September 16, Fonteno posted an Instagram comment responding to a clip of the podcast: "I just talked to Kai and it was an honest mistake and it's fixed. Thanks @kaicenat" .
Kai Cenat has not publicly commented on the situation, so the resolution is entirely from Fonteno's account .
Discussion Prompt
GTA 5's Franklin actor called out Kai Cenat over a broken promise to a kid, then squashed it a day later. Do you think a quick private conversation is enough, or does the public nature of the callout demand a public apology from Kai?
Note
This post is based on reports from IGN, Dexerto, and other outlets from September 15-16, 2026 .
